The 30-share BSE Sensex slipped 8.08 points, or 0.01 per cent, to close at 73,598.67, with 17 constituents higher, 12 lower and one unchanged. During the day, it hit a high of 73,762.98 and a low of 73,179.41.
The 50-share NSE Nifty skidded 3.45 points, or 0.02 per cent, to end at 22,749.75.

items.title: Mankind Pharma Q2 profit rises 38% to Rs 716 crore
items.summary: Mankind Pharma has announced a profit increase of 37.7% to ₹716 crore during the September quarter. Revenue from operations rose to ₹4,337.9 crore compared to ₹3,697.2 crore in the same quarter last year. This growth is attributed to strong performance in both domestic and international markets. The recent acquisition of Armed Cell Therapeutics is expected to enhance R&D capabilities.

items.title: Tata consumer Q2 net profit up despite higher costs, weak tea demand
items.summary: Tata Consumer Products encountered unchanged tea volumes and decreasing revenue in the September quarter as weak demand and surging commodity costs took their toll. To counter this, the company emphasized its salt business, which saw significant revenue increases driven by volume growth and price hikes. Meanwhile, international revenue held steady despite challenges in the UK market caused by weather issues.

items.title: SBI launches CyRIS centre to strengthen cybersecurity capabilities
items.summary: SBI proudly introduces CyRIS, its new Cybersecurity Centre of Excellence, designed to elevate digital protection and competence. This centre will delve into vital aspects like threat intelligence, cyber defense mechanisms, and ethical hacking practices. It also emphasizes malware analysis, AI security, and quantum-safe advances, showcasing SBI's unwavering resolve to fortify cybersecurity across the financial landscape through collaborative efforts.

items.title: NBFCs curb fresh loans in rural markets as weak monsoon raises repayment risks
items.summary: India's leading non-bank lenders like Shriram Finance and Bajaj Finance are limiting new lending in drought-affected regions. The lenders are closely monitoring borrowers for early signs of repayment difficulties due to weak monsoon rainfall. Companies are adjusting loan growth expectations downward and strengthening collection efforts in impacted locations. Several states are under close scrutiny as economic pressures mount from lower incomes and agricultural yields.

Analysts suggest that Indian stock markets will trade sideways until there is greater clarity on global developments. items.title: Stocks in news: Paytm, Tata Consumer, Dalmia Bharat, REC and DCM Shriram
items.summary: Indian equity markets showed recovery with a rise in NSE Nifty 50, ending a four-session losing streak. Several companies reported their September-quarter earnings, highlighting varying financial performances. Paytm experienced significant profit growth, while Dalmia Bharat reported a net loss due to an exceptional charge. Defence stocks are also in focus following government procurement approvals. Investors continue to track earnings reports and related developments in the market.

items.title: Jio IPO delivers smaller payday for bankers than other mega offerings
items.summary: In a landmark move, Jio Platforms, supported by Mukesh Ambani, successfully secured ₹30,213 crore, marking the largest IPO in India’s history. Investment bankers were rewarded with ₹196 crore in fees, translating to only 0.65% of the total amount raised. In contrast, Hyundai Motor India achieved ₹27,859 crore while paying out a heftier ₹493 crore in fees, which amount to 1.77%.

items.title: Indian markets rebound, but rising oil prices keep investors cautious
items.summary: On Monday, Indian equity markets staged a comeback following four days of losses, with both the BSE Sensex and NSE Nifty seeing notable gains as investors sought to take advantage of cheaper stock prices. However, analysts warn that this recovery is precarious, influenced by global geopolitical issues and high crude oil prices.

items.title: Retail investors return to equities with Rs 10,572 crore buying in September
items.summary: After two months of silence, September marked the return of retail investors to the secondary market, as they invested ₹10,572 crore in equities. This shift occurred after a significant market dip linked to escalating oil prices. In contrast, foreign portfolio investors continued their exit strategy. Additionally, the primary market thrived with ₹5,650 crore in shares bought by retail investors, emphasizing that upcoming market conditions will shape their future involvement.

items.title: Rising concentration in AI stocks poses a risk: Kunal Kapoor, Morningstar CEO
items.summary: Kunal Kapoor, the CEO of Morningstar, voiced unease about the dangers of focusing investments heavily on AI stocks during his Mumbai trip. He stressed that lofty expectations might not always reflect in company profits, potentially leading to disappointing market outcomes. While praising India's compelling growth story, he remarked that its investment valuations do not stand up favorably against those in emerging markets.

items.title: Govt seeks investor and expert views on LTCG and STT as it reviews capital market levies amid FPI exodus
items.summary: The government has initiated a reassessment of long-term capital gains tax and securities transaction tax. Stakeholders, including investors and tax experts, have been consulted for their views. The debate has gained momentum due to significant outflows of foreign portfolio investments. Current taxation methods may affect the attractiveness of Indian equities compared to global markets. The upcoming budget provides an opportunity to revisit these tax regulations.

items.title: Noel Tata renews challenge to Chandrasekaran’s reappointment, questions Tata Sons board voting and conflict of interest
items.summary: Noel Tata has raised concerns about N Chandrasekaran's reappointment as executive chairman of Tata Sons. His objections relate to board procedures, including voting requirements and potential conflicts of interest. The board approved Chandrasekaran's position despite Noel Tata's requests for detailed meeting records. Additionally, he questioned the legitimacy of the meeting agenda and the absence of a selection committee.

items.title: India earns nearly 50% more from fuel exports in April-September as costlier oil and weak rupee outweigh lower volumes
items.summary: India's petroleum product export earnings increased significantly in April to September, driven by high international prices. While the volume of shipments declined by 16%, earnings surged by nearly 50% in rupee terms. Diesel exports were the largest contributors to the earnings growth, accounting for 42% of the total volume. Both diesel and petrol consumption rose during this period, whereas production saw slight declines.
